ca_emigrant_wall.blurb: Emigrant Wall is a long, gentle-angled wall in the Silver Lake basin, off Highway 88 west of Kirkwood in the Eldorado National Forest. It is the basin's multi-pitch option, and it suits climbers stepping up from single-pitch cragging. Most of the 16 climbs are bolted sport lines with a few trad routes, and the grades are easy to moderate, from the low 5th class up to about 5.9. Routes typically run three or four pitches, and long pitches mean a 70 m rope is handy. The wall catches sun for most of the day, so bases can feel warm while the upper pitches get a breeze. Expect a real walk in through woods and across granite slab.

ca_orange_pillar.blurb: Orange Pillar is a crack climber's buttress in Patricia Bowl, up Rock Creek in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 10,800 feet. All 16 climbs are trad, mostly finger-to-hand-sized cracks and corners, with grades running from 5.7 up to a single 5.12, though the bulk sit around 5.10 and 5.11. The rock has an orange tint and faces south and east, so it picks up good morning sun. Some pitches higher on the formation have loose rock, so wear a helmet. The approach crosses scree that can be treacherous early in the summer. A smaller buttress below holds more single-pitch crack lines.

ca_mosquito_coast.blurb: Mosquito Coast is a short, steep cliff beside the South Fork of the American River, directly beneath a road bridge near Placerville. The wall is only 30 to 40 feet tall and mostly overhanging, with smooth, water-polished stone and cracks in every width. Of the 16 climbs, most are trad or top-rope crack lines, graded mainly 5.10 and 5.11, with a few boulder problems along the base where a pad helps with the hard landings. Summers run hot, so go early or late in the day; the cooler seasons work better midday, though winter ice and spring runoff can shut things down.

ca_lower_flumes_formation.blurb: The Lower Flumes Formation is the base section of the Flumes cliff on the west side of Pinnacles National Park, a short hike up from the trailhead. It holds 16 climbs, mostly bolted single pitches plus one two-pitch line, a couple of trad lines and a top rope. The grades are friendly: a few easy routes, then a cluster at 5.9 and a couple at 5.10a. It suits intermediate leaders and is quieter than the park's east side, with a more remote feel.

ca_john_yablonski_rock.blurb: John Yablonski Rock is the big central pile of boulders just south of Cap Rock in Joshua Tree National Park, a short stroll from the Cap Rock parking area and reached along the nature trail that loops around it. Most of the 16 climbs here are trad, with a couple of sport routes and top ropes, and the grades range widely from easy fourth-class and low 5th terrain up through 5.10 and 5.11. Because the routes are close to the trail and easy to identify, it makes a handy stop for a few quick pitches rather than a full-day destination.

ca_b_north_face.blurb: The North Face is the lowest-angle side of Tahquitz Rock above Idyllwild, at roughly 7,400 feet. All 16 climbs are trad, running from about 5.5 to 5.11, with a good number of moderate lines. Routes go up to about six pitches, following long crack systems and dihedrals, with newer lines up the slabs between. The rock is better low down and looser higher up, so avoid climbing beneath another party. The face stays cool and committing compared with the sunny south side, and longer routes finish on the northeast shoulder, followed by third-class ground and the North Gully back to the base.

ca_north_dome.blurb: North Dome is a huge white wall on the north side of Kings Canyon, near the end of the road at Cedar Grove, with faces rising around 1,500 feet. Sometimes called the El Cap of Kings Canyon, it offers long grade V free climbs and big aid lines, plus shorter slab and crack routes on the arched base. The 16 listed climbs split between trad and aid, with free grades mostly 5.10 to 5.11. Allow up to 45 minutes to reach the base. The lower wall can bake at midday.

ca_upper_bulge_routes.blurb: The Upper Bulge is the steep, tooth-shaped section midway up the west face of Tahquitz Rock, above Idyllwild. From below it looks smooth, but it holds some of the hardest sustained climbing on the formation. The 16 climbs are mostly trad, with a couple of aid lines, graded from 5.7 through 5.12, though the core sits between 5.10 and 5.12. Routes are short for Tahquitz, typically three or four pitches, and feel notably exposed. Most lines start from the big gully on the right, then work up to ledges below the bulge. The descent is down the friction route.
